translation:
  text: '“Explain something further to me, sir,” I said. “What do you want to know?”
    he said. “Why, sir,” I said, “did the stones come up from the depths and get placed
    in the building, when they had already worn these spirits?”


    2. “They had to come up through water,” he said, “so that they might be made alive.
    For they could not otherwise enter God’s kingdom unless they put off the deadness
    of their former life.[a]”


    3. “So these people who had fallen asleep also received the seal of the Son of
    God and entered God’s kingdom.[b] For before a person bears the name of the Son
    of God, that person is dead. But on receiving the seal, the person puts off deadness
    and takes up life.”


    4. “The seal, then, is the water.[c] They go down into the water dead and come
    up alive. This seal was therefore proclaimed to those people too, and they made
    use of it so that they might enter God’s kingdom.”


    5. “Why, sir,” I said, “did the forty stones also come up from the depths with
    them, when they already had the seal?” “Because,” he said, “these apostles and
    teachers who proclaimed the name of the Son of God, after falling asleep in the
    power and faith of the Son of God, also proclaimed to those who had fallen asleep
    before them. They themselves gave them the seal of the proclamation.”


    6. “So they went down with them into the water and came up again. But these went
    down alive and came up alive again; those who had fallen asleep before them went
    down dead but came up alive.[d]”


    7. “Through these, then, they were made alive and came to know the name of the
    Son of God. That is why they also came up with them and were fitted into the building
    of the tower. They were built together without being hewn, for they had fallen
    asleep in righteousness and great purity. They lacked only this seal. Now you
    also have the explanation about these people.”[e] “I have it, sir,” I said.'

  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: “Former” is bracketed in the printed Greek, supplied from the versions as
      reported. Sinaiticus partly preserves a corresponding first/former-life expression,
      with damage in the paragraph. The necessity and unless condition are retained.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The entry-into-the-kingdom sentence is bar-marked as an insertion in the
      older working edition, reported missing in Athos by similar endings. It is now
      attested in the primary Sinaiticus transcription,Q95F8r col4 lines8–14, as entry
      into “the kingdom of the Son of God.” The draft retains the printed “God’s kingdom”;
      alternative: “They entered the kingdom of the Son of God.” The next printed
      “of the Son” phrase is bracketed and also occurs in Sinaiticus. This corroboration
      is specific to these phrases, not a full adoption of Sinaiticus.'
  - marker: c
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The source itself identifies the seal as water and describes descent dead
      and ascent alive. This is baptismal imagery in the vision; the draft does not
      replace the narrated actions with a later doctrinal explanation or insert the
      word Hades.
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The older edition supplies the entire contrast from Clement of Alexandria’s
      quotation, with an inner bracket around “and came up alive again.” Bounded comparison
      of Clement, Stromata2.9.44.2–3,1906 printed136, supports retaining that inner
      phrase. Sinaiticus also has the contrast, with some supplied letters, but its
      apostles’ ascent reads “and came up again,” without a repeated “alive”; alternative:
      “But these went down alive and came up again; those who had fallen asleep before
      them went down dead but came up alive.” These are separate transmission routes,
      not unanimous wording. The Clement editor’s corrections elsewhere from Hermas
      are not independent manuscript evidence.'
  - marker: e
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Through these” keeps the source’s plural expression rather than inserting
      a new named agent. The speakers distinguish the apostles/teachers from those
      who died earlier; the draft preserves the vision’s proclamation, seal and life
      language without extending its scope beyond the described groups.

  yaml_path: translation/extra_canonical/shepherd_of_hermas/093.yaml
  text: '“Explain something further to me, sir,” I said. “What do you want to know?” he said. “Why, sir,”
    I said, “did the stones come up from the depths and get placed in the building, when they had already
    worn these spirits?”


    2. “They had to come up through water,” he said, “so that they might be made alive. For they could
    not otherwise enter God’s kingdom unless they put off the deadness of their former life.[a]”


    3. “So these people who had fallen asleep also received the seal of the Son of God and entered God’s
    kingdom.[b] For before a person bears the name of the Son of God, that person is dead. But on receiving
    the seal, the person puts off deadness and takes up life.”


    4. “The seal, then, is the water.[c] They go down into the water dead and come up alive. This seal
    was therefore proclaimed to those people too, and they made use of it so that they might enter God’s
    kingdom.”


    5. “Why, sir,” I said, “did the forty stones also come up from the depths with them, when they already
    had the seal?” “Because,” he said, “these apostles and teachers who proclaimed the name of the Son
    of God, after falling asleep in the power and faith of the Son of God, also proclaimed to those who
    had fallen asleep before them. They themselves gave them the seal of the proclamation.”


    6. “So they went down with them into the water and came up again. But these went down alive and came
    up alive again; those who had fallen asleep before them went down dead but came up alive.[d]”


    7. “Through these, then, they were made alive and came to know the name of the Son of God. That is
    why they also came up with them and were fitted into the building of the tower. They were built together
    without being hewn, for they had fallen asleep in righteousness and great purity. They lacked only
    this seal. Now you also have the explanation about these people.”[e] “I have it, sir,” I said.'
